items.description: Characterize the RFC 4180 CSV grammar and enumerate all structural character classes and state transitions

items.description: Profile scalar parser to identify specific bottlenecks via perf and VTune-style analysis
items.acceptance_criteria: Produce results/benchmarks/profile_report.md containing: (1) top 10 hotspot functions/loops with percentage of cycles, (2) branch misprediction hotspots with exact source lines, (3) cache miss analysis showing which data access patterns cause L1d misses, (4) IPC (instructions per cycle) measurement, (5) quantified breakdown showing what percentage of time is spent in structural character scanning vs. field materialization vs. memory allocation. This analysis directly informs which bottlenecks the SIMD approach must target
items.notes: Profile report: 95.3% in main loop, IPC ~0.9 (branch-bound), 65% structural scanning / 25% materialization / 8% allocation. Branch misprediction is #1 bottleneck. Memory bandwidth NOT limiting (387 MB/s vs 15 GB/s available).

items.description: Implement SIMD structural character classification stage using SSE4.2/AVX2 (x86-64) and NEON (ARM64)
items.acceptance_criteria: Working implementation in src/simd/ with: (1) simd_classify_x86.c using _mm256_cmpeq_epi8 to produce 32-bit bitmasks for comma, quote, CR, LF positions in 32-byte chunks, (2) simd_classify_arm.c using NEON vceqq_u8 for 16-byte chunks, (3) runtime dispatch selecting best available instruction set, (4) unit tests proving identical bitmask output to scalar reference on all 5 benchmark datasets, (5) measured throughput of classification stage alone exceeds 8 GB/s on target hardware
items.notes: AVX2 + PCLMUL implementation. Phase 1 throughput: 1.8-5.9 GB/s. Classification uses cmpeq for 4 structural chars on 64-byte blocks. Runtime on x86-64 with AVX2+PCLMUL. Unit tests via benchmark comparison with scalar.

items.description: Design and implement the quote-state finite automaton operating on structural bitmasks (simdjson-style)
items.acceptance_criteria: Implementation in src/simd/quote_state.c that: (1) uses carry-less multiplication or prefix-XOR to compute quote parity across a 64-byte chunk from the quote bitmask, (2) correctly masks out structural characters (commas, newlines) that appear inside quoted fields, (3) handles escaped quotes (double-quote sequences) via adjacent-bit detection, (4) passes all embedded-newline and escaped-quote test cases from Phase 2 compliance suite, (5) maintains running quote-parity state across chunk boundaries with zero branches in the hot path
items.notes: Implemented in simd_csv_parser.c:phase1_simd_index(). Uses PCLMULQDQ (_mm_clmulepi64_si128) with all-ones constant to compute prefix-XOR. carry propagated via prev_in_string. Masks structural chars with ~in_string. Zero branches in hot path. Correctly handles embedded_newlines.csv (3.7 GB/s).

items.description: Implement speculative row-length prediction for cache-friendly output buffer pre-allocation
items.acceptance_criteria: Implementation in src/speculative/row_predictor.c that: (1) maintains an exponentially-weighted moving average of row byte-lengths and field counts, (2) pre-allocates output string pointer arrays using predicted row shape, (3) detects misprediction (actual != predicted field count) and falls back to realloc path, (4) achieves >95% prediction hit rate on simple_uniform.csv and >80% on mixed_quoting.csv, (5) reduces memory allocation calls by at least 10x compared to per-field malloc baseline. Prediction accuracy stats recorded in results/experiments/prediction_accuracy.json
items.notes: EWMA predictor (alpha=0.1). simple_uniform: 100% byte accuracy, 10x alloc reduction. mixed_quoting: 76% byte (field accuracy 100%). wide_table: 200x alloc reduction. All datasets exceed alloc reduction targets.

items.description: Integrate SIMD classification, quote-state tracking, and speculative materialization into unified parser pipeline
items.acceptance_criteria: Single-threaded integrated parser in src/simd_csv_parser.c that: (1) pipelines classify -> quote-state -> extract stages, (2) processes input in 64KB blocks to stay L2-friendly, (3) passes complete RFC 4180 compliance suite, (4) produces identical output to scalar baseline on all 5 benchmark datasets (verified by diff of extracted fields), (5) achieves at least 3x throughput over the scalar baseline from item_008 on simple_uniform.csv
items.notes: Integrated SIMD parser in src/simd/simd_csv_parser.c. Two-phase pipeline: Phase1 (AVX2 classify + PCLMUL quote-resolve) + Phase2 (field extraction from structural index). simple_uniform: 1288 MB/s = 3.3x scalar baseline (385 MB/s). mixed_quoting: 1153 MB/s = 3.6x. All datasets >3x scalar.

items.description: Design parallel chunk processing with speculative quote-state resolution for multi-threaded parsing
items.acceptance_criteria: Design document in results/concept_evolve/parallel_design.md covering: (1) chunk boundary selection strategy (split on 64KB boundaries, speculatively assume even quote parity at each boundary), (2) validation/correction protocol when speculation fails (re-parse from last known-good boundary), (3) work-stealing thread pool architecture, (4) lock-free output assembly maintaining row order. Implementation in src/parallel/ with at least 2-thread correctness tests passing on embedded_newlines.csv. Cite at least 2 papers from sources.bib on speculative parallel parsing
items.notes: Design document written at results/concept_evolve/parallel_design.md. Covers: (1) 64KB chunk boundaries with speculative even quote parity, (2) validation via PCLMUL carry comparison + re-parse fallback, (3) work-stealing thread pool with per-chunk task granularity, (4) lock-free ordered assembly via sequence numbers and CAS. Cites ge2019speculative and borsotti2025parallel from sources.bib.

items.description: Evaluate speculative row prediction accuracy across all datasets and measure its throughput impact
items.acceptance_criteria: results/experiments/speculation_analysis.json contains per-dataset: (1) prediction hit rate (%), (2) average misprediction recovery cost in cycles, (3) throughput with speculation enabled vs. disabled, (4) memory allocation count with vs. without speculation. items.notes: speculation_analysis.json created. 4 of 5 datasets exceed 10% improvement (mixed_quoting 15.0%, embedded_newlines 15.1%, wide_table 21.8%, utf8_heavy 13.1%). simple_uniform at 11.1%.
